mechanism_narrative: If WORKPLACES keeps edging up from its recent trough while TRANSIT stays less negative, commuter circulation should widen weekday shopping trips and lift RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks. The signal is stronger when RESIDENTIAL does not rise materially at the same time.
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES improved from -10.6 to -8.6 while TRANSIT stayed around -22 to -25 and RETAIL_REC remained weak
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not rise above its prior 4-week mean even though WORKPLACES improves for two consecutive weeks and TRANSIT is not more negative than -25.

mechanism_narrative: A further drop in TRANSIT below the recent range will reduce spontaneous downtown shopping visits and pull RETAIL_REC lower within one to two weeks. This mechanism fails if transit worsens but retail improves anyway, implying offsetting non-commute trip generation.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT falls below -25 after having been above -25 in the previous week
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT moved from -21.3 to -24.6 and then -22.4 while RETAIL_REC fell from -13.3 to -17.9
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC increases over the next week despite TRANSIT crossing below -25 from a higher prior value.

mechanism_narrative: When PARKS activity collapses after a brief rebound, discretionary out-of-home time shifts away from leisure districts and retail visits weaken over the following two weeks. The effect should be clearest if GROCERY_PHARM stays stable and does not absorb the displaced trips.
candidate_trigger: PARKS declines by more than 10 points week-on-week from a positive level
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS fell from 26.1 to 10.6 to 4.6 while GROCERY_PHARM stayed near +8 to +10 and RETAIL_REC fell to -17.9
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not decline within two weeks after a >10-point weekly drop in PARKS from a positive level.

mechanism_narrative: If RESIDENTIAL demand stays elevated while WORKPLACES remain suppressed, people are more likely to substitute home-centered activity for shopping trips, keeping RETAIL_REC below its recent average over four weeks. The mechanism breaks if mobility reopens enough that commuting and shopping rise together.
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL stayed above baseline near +4 while WORKPLACES stayed below baseline near -9 to -11 and RETAIL_REC moved lower
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises above the prior 4-week mean while RESIDENTIAL remains at or above +3 and WORKPLACES remains at or below -8.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in PARKS during late-winter to early-spring weeks acts as a leading sign of broader discretionary outing recovery, which should lift RETAIL_REC within four weeks. The effect is strongest when TRANSIT is also recovering rather than deteriorating.
candidate_trigger: PARKS turns up for two consecutive weeks from a level above 10
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS was 14.3 then 26.1 before dropping to 4.6 while RETAIL_REC trended downward
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC remains flat or declines over the next 28 days after PARKS posts two consecutive weekly increases from above 10.

mechanism_narrative: When GROCERY_PHARM rises while RETAIL_REC falls, households are reallocating trips toward essential shopping, and that substitution should keep discretionary retail weaker over the next one to two weeks. The signal fails if grocery gains are accompanied by a retail rebound.
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM increased from 8.1 to 9.6 while RETAIL_REC fell from -13.3 to -17.9
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises over the next two weeks despite GROCERY_PHARM holding above +9 and continuing to increase.

mechanism_narrative: A sharper divergence between TRANSIT and WORKPLACES indicates mobility restrictions or cautious commuting that suppresses discretionary shopping and pushes RETAIL_REC lower over the next four weeks. The mechanism requires transit to remain materially below baseline while workplaces do not recover above -5.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT stays below -20 for two straight weeks while WORKPLACES stays below -5
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT hovered around -22 to -25 and WORKPLACES around -8 to -11 while RETAIL_REC weakened
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC increases over the next 28 days even though TRANSIT remains below -20 and WORKPLACES remains below -5.

mechanism_narrative: If RESIDENTIAL eases back toward baseline without a matching rebound in WORKPLACES, some home-based activity is replaced by local errands and short shopping trips, producing a modest RETAIL_REC improvement within one week. The claim fails if home stay remains elevated or if workplace mobility also rises strongly.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL falls below +3 after being at or above +4
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL was 4.1, 3.7, 3.4, then 4.0 while WORKPLACES improved only slightly and RETAIL_REC kept falling
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not improve within one week after RESIDENTIAL drops below +3.
